feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Start: "construction of the Main Injector synchrotron and Recycler storage ring was initiated and completed in the spring of 1999 with the Main Injector initially utilized in the last Tevatron fixed target run" (Shiltsev). End: "Run II was initiated in March of 2001 and continued through September 2011" and "The Tevatron will be shut off September 30, 2011." (same paper). The P1 and A1 lines carried the proton and antiproton injection from the Main Injector to the Tevatron (NuMI paper). Before 1999 the Tevatron was injected by the Fermilab Main Ring, which has no Atlas record.
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: Protons from the Booster and antiprotons from the Recycler were accelerated to 150 GeV in the Main Injector

intervals.label: federal funding approved
intervals.locator: press release of 1 June 1999, paragraph on the history of the project
intervals.note: Start at month precision: the Fermilab dedication release says federal funding was approved in October 1991 (an Illinois challenge grant of 1991 had already paid for environmental and design studies). The end is the groundbreaking of the next interval.
intervals.quote: Federal funding for the project was approved in October 1991, and construction got underway in 1993, after extensive R&D.

intervals.label: construction
intervals.locator: Fermilab History and Archives, page 'Accelerator History', section 'Main Injector'
intervals.note: Groundbreaking on 22 March 1993 (Fermilab History and Archives); the dedication release likewise says construction 'got underway in 1993'. The Main Injector Technical Design Handbook (Chapter 1, PDF p. 5) says "Construction on the FMI project was initiated in June, 1992." and the PAC 1999 paper says the project received first funding in FY92, so project work (design, procurement, R&D) began before the 1993 groundbreaking of the tunnel. Ring civil construction was finished in 1997 and the ring's technical components were installed by 1998; beamline construction towards the Tevatron began in September 1997 and installation continued into late 1998 (PAC 1999 paper, section 1). The end is the start of ring commissioning (next interval). The start's earliest bound, 1992-06, is the handbook's statement.
intervals.quote: The lab broke ground on the Main Injector on March 22, 1993.

intervals.label: ring commissioning (weekend beam studies)
intervals.locator: PAC 1999 paper MOCL3, §2 'Commissioning schedule'; PDF p. 1 (proceedings p. 31)
intervals.note: Ring commissioning began in September 1998 on weekends only, while installation continued during the week. The paper dates the 120 GeV and 150 GeV commissioning goals to 27 and 28 November (year not printed there; the paper was written for PAC 1999 in March 1999). The end is the dedication of 1 June 1999 (next interval).
intervals.quote: The commissioning of the Main Injector (MI) ring began in September 1998.

intervals.label: operating (dedicated 1 June 1999)
intervals.locator: start: Fermilab press release of 1 June 1999 (dateline 'June 1'); end: see the following interval (Fermilab PAC report, April 2026 meeting, findings on accelerator status)
intervals.note: Start is the dedication of 1 June 1999 ("It was dedicated on June 1, 1999.", Fermilab History and Archives; the release says the machine 'officially began its life'; the history page adds that it began delivering protons to the Tevatron in 1999); beams had been accelerated in the ring since the commissioning weekends of 1998 (previous interval). Collider (Run II) operation started in March 2001 and NuMI data taking on 20 May 2005. The end is sourced to "The MI has not operated since July 2024" (Fermilab PAC, April 2026 meeting) and "Following the record achievement [1.018 MW to NuMI, June 2024], the Main Injector complex suffered a series of failures that have prevented NuMI beam." (IPAC'26). The start is the dedication ceremony (the interval is marked 'approximate'), not the first beam delivered to the Tevatron, which the history page dates only to 1999.

intervals.label: last reported: no Main Injector beam
intervals.locator: Fermilab PAC report April 2026; PAC NuMI mini-meeting report July 2025 ("There was no beam delivery for MI since 2024"); PDF p. 2 of the April 2026 PAC report
intervals.note: Last reported beam condition; restart is not confirmed in the Atlas source audit on 2026-11-19. The open end retains the last reported condition as an assumption, not a new observation that the shutdown persisted. The April 2026 PAC report says MI had not operated since July 2024; the Fall 2026 report (PDF pages 4-5) still describes stable beam on 1 October as planned and the restart as upcoming. The proposed NuMI run remains a separate planned interval. A later report of operation should close this interval; passing a scheduled date must not do so.
intervals.quote: The MI has not operated since July 2024

intervals.label: NuMI run (planned: 12 weeks, stretch goal 20)
intervals.locator: Fall 2026 PAC report, PDF page 4, accelerator-complex findings (FY27 run and planned stable beam); April 2026 report, PDF page 3, stretch schedule
intervals.note: A schedule, not a reported event. The Fall 2026 PAC report plans 12 weeks of FY27 operation, with a stretch goal of 20 weeks; stable MI beam was planned for 1 October 2026. The February 2027 end retains the April report stretch schedule. The source audit on 2026-11-19 found no later confirmation of this run in the reviewed primary sources.
intervals.quote: The plan is for 12 weeks of operation in FY27, with a stretch goal of 20 weeks of operation, with a focus on the NuMI beam.

intervals.label: Tevatron injector (150 GeV)
intervals.note: While injecting the Tevatron the Main Injector accelerated to 150 GeV, its design energy; the neutrino-production operating point is 120 GeV (top-level beam_energy).
intervals.quote: Protons from the Booster and antiprotons from the Recycler were accelerated to 150 GeV in the Main Injector

beam_energy.quote: Protons from the Booster and antiprotons from the Recycler were accelerated to 150 GeV in the Main Injector

name: Fermilab Main Injector
notes: Design energy 150 GeV per the NuMI beam paper; 120 GeV is the neutrino-production operating point.

beam_energy.locator: §2 NuMI Beam Components, first paragraph; arXiv PDF p. 6
beam_energy.note: Operating energy for neutrino production; the design energy is 150 GeV.
beam_energy.quote: The NuMI beam is presently the world's most powerful neutrino beam and is produced by the 120 GeV protons extracted from the Fermilab Main Injector.

circumference.locator: §5 Post-MINOS Plans and Developments; arXiv PDF p. 60
circumference.quote: The Recycler is a fixed energy machine of 8 GeV located on the top of the MI with the same circumference of 3.3 km.

injection_energy.note: Protons from the 8 GeV Booster (and, in Tevatron Run II, antiprotons from the 8 GeV Recycler).
injection_energy.quote: This accelerator would use the Fermilab 8 GeV Booster as an injector and have the ability to accelerate protons up to 150 GeV

summary.plain: A 3.3-kilometre ring that accelerates protons to 120 billion electronvolts. Its beam makes the NuMI neutrinos and will make the LBNF beam for DUNE, but it has not operated since July 2024; a restart was planned for October 2026.
summary.technical: 3.3 km circumference proton synchrotron, design energy 150 GeV, operated at 120 GeV for neutrino production; slip-stacked Booster batches are loaded via the Recycler. Source of the NuMI beam and of the future LBNF beam.
